prompt.context: Our client is a major US television network. The Winter Olympics are a huge deal and will require a significant amount of capital to secure the broadcasting rights. The client is trying to figure out how much to bid for the exclusive right to broadcast the 2022 Winter Olympics Games in the U.S.
prompt.question: How much should our client bid for the exclusive right to broadcast the 2022 Winter Olympics in the U.S.? Determine the appropriate bid amount after considering all relevant factors.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any subscription revenue available?
clarifying_info.a: No subscription revenue, but the network can keep 100% of advertising revenue.
$400K per 30-second ad for prime time (Monday-Friday 7-11 PM, and all weekend) and $200K per ad for non-prime time.

clarifying_info.q: How much advertising time is allowed per hour?
clarifying_info.a: Market research shows no more than 10 minutes of advertising per hour.

clarifying_info.q: Is there an opportunity cost to consider?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, $1M per hour of air time used for the Olympics (opportunity cost of not airing other content).

clarifying_info.q: What discount rate or WACC should we use?
clarifying_info.a: WACC is 10%. There is also a 4-year lag for receipt of revenue.

exhibits.title: Winter Olympics Schedule
exhibits.shows: A schedule showing the broadcast windows for each phase of the Winter Olympics: Day 1 (Opening Ceremonies on Friday), Days 2-15 (weekdays and weekends), and Day 16 (Closing Ceremonies on Saturday), with specific time slots for each.

framework: Define the problem as a cost-benefit / NPV analysis: determine if expected profits justify the bid
Identify all revenue streams: advertising revenue is the primary (and only) revenue source
Calculate total broadcast hours by segment: Opening/Closing Ceremonies, Weekday prime, Weekday non-prime, Weekend
Apply ad rates and ad density (10 min/hr max, 2 x 30-sec slots per minute) to get total revenue
Identify and quantify all costs: production costs, opportunity costs, and time value of money (discount rate)
Calculate NPV = (Revenue - Production Costs - Opportunity Costs) / Discount Factor
Layer in qualitative / intangible factors that could push bid above or below NPV
State a final bid recommendation with justification

questions.prompt: Calculate the total revenue from broadcasting the Winter Olympics.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use the schedule to identify four broadcast segments: (1) Weekday prime time, (2) Weekday non-prime time, (3) Weekend, (4) Opening and Closing Ceremonies. For each segment, multiply: days x hours/day x 10 min/hr x 2 ad slots/min x ad rate. Sum all four segments.

math.setup: Revenue = days x hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x rate/ad. Prime time rate = $400K, non-prime rate = $200K.
steps: Weekday prime (M-F, 7-11pm): 10 weekdays x 4 hrs x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400K = $320M
Weekday non-prime (M-F, 9am-12pm + 2-5pm = 6 hrs): 10 weekdays x 6 hrs x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $200K = $240M
Weekend (11am-9pm = 10 hrs/day, 4 weekend days): 4 days x 10 hrs x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400K = $320M
Opening/Closing Ceremonies (2 days x 3 hrs, prime rate): 2 days x 3 hrs x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400K = $48M

questions.prompt: Factoring in all costs, calculate the project profit and then the NPV. Is this a good investment?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify three cost components: (1) production costs ($482M), (2) opportunity cost ($1M/hr x total broadcast hours), and (3) time value of money using WACC=10% over 4 years. Profit = Revenue - Production Costs - Opportunity Costs. NPV = Profit / discount factor.

math.setup: Profit = Revenue - Production Costs - Opportunity Costs. NPV = Profit / (1 + WACC)^4. Total hours = Opening/Closing (2 x 3 = 6 hrs) + Weekdays (10 x 10 = 100 hrs) + Weekends (4 x 10 = 40 hrs) = 146 hrs.
steps: Opportunity cost: 146 total broadcast hours x $1M/hr = $146M
math.answer: NPV = $200M; this is a positive-NPV investment.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the NPV of $200M, what intangible factors, benefits, and risks should the network consider when deciding how much to bid?

categories.name: Strategic / Brand Benefits
ideas: Prestige and brand elevation from hosting a marquee global event
Access to new viewers who may become loyal to the network
Opportunity to promote other network programming during Olympics air time
Strengthened relationships with advertisers and sponsors

categories.name: Supplemental Revenue Opportunities
ideas: Product tie-ins and sponsorship packages beyond standard ad slots
Digital streaming and online rights revenue
Highlight packages and on-demand content licensing

categories.name: Competitive / Game Theory Considerations
ideas: Rival networks also bidding — final bid must exceed competitors' willingness to pay
Winning the bid prevents a competitor from gaining the same brand and viewer benefits
Bidding too low risks losing; bidding too high destroys value

categories.name: Risks
ideas: Revenue uncertainty if viewership is lower than projected
Athlete scandal or geopolitical events reducing viewership
Regulatory or IOC restrictions on ad content or format

recommendation: The maximum rational bid is approximately $200M, reflecting the NPV of projected cash flows after production and opportunity costs, discounted at WACC over the 4-year revenue lag.

Intangible benefits — new viewer acquisition, programming promotion, and brand prestige — provide justification to bid at or slightly above $200M, but significant deviation requires strong quantitative justification.
risks: Viewership shortfall reducing actual ad revenue below projections
Competitive overbidding driven by game theory dynamics pushing bid beyond intrinsic value
Production cost overruns eroding the $300M profit margin
next_steps: Model sensitivity of bid to viewership assumptions (e.g., what if ad revenue is 20% lower?)
Assess competitor networks’ likely bid ranges to inform game theory strategy
Quantify the incremental value of new viewer acquisition and programming promotion to determine how much above NPV the bid can be justified
